newsitem.title: USA: Missing Irish girl found alive in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Missing Irish girl found alive in Florida.

text.p: A four-year-old girl from Northern Ireland who vanished from her family's Florida hotel room was found along a roadside about 15 miles (24 km) from the hotel on Monday about 20 hours after she went missing, police said.
"They found her," said Jim Solomons, a spokesman for the Orange County Sheriff's Department shortly after Caoimhe McEvoy was located at 2:10 p.m. EDT (1810 GMT).

Police said the girl appeared to be in good condition, but that they were awaiting a hospital report for definite word. They suspected the child had been kidnapped and said it was too early to discuss whether she had been abused or assaulted.

"Obviously, she didn't walk that far. We're believing she was abducted and driven there. We now need to have her medically checked out to see if there was any type of foul play," said Steve Jones, another sheriff's department spokesman.

Caoimhe was found by a nurse who stopped her car after driving by, called police and stayed with the child until they arrived. Caoimhe, from Belfast in Northern Ireland, was taken to Orlando Regional Medical Centre for examination.

Patricia Wilson Hart, the nurse who discovered the child, told reporters she noticed the girl walking too close to the road. "She said, 'Where's my daddy?' That broke my heart," said Hart, who added she had other information about the girl that police asked her to withhold from reporters.

Brown-haired, brown-eyed Caoimhe had disappeared from her family's hotel rooms at the Quality Inn on International Drive in the middle of Orlando's tourist district at about 6 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT) on Sunday, as the family packed their bags at the end of a two-week vacation, Orange County Deputy Mike Pagan said.
Hundreds of law officers had searched for her all night and into the day on Monday. Tourists and local residents had distributed flyers bearing her image to assist in the search.
Earlier, McEvoy's parents -- looking tense and teary-eyed -- had begged quietly for the child's return.
After hearing on television that she had been found alive, Gerard and Mary McEvoy said they were ecstatic.

"Over the moon. Over the moon. I just love everybody here honestly," said Mrs McEvoy when asked to describe her feelings. Gerard McEvoy said, "I just can't thank them all enough. at noon I wasn't too optimistic at all... I don't believe it."

Police were continuing their investigation on Monday night. Jones said investigators were questioning several people that might have information on the case, but no arrest had been made. Police earlier had said they considered anyone acting suspicious in the area a potential suspect.
